races.name: Download The Raceday Ready App Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Merit Estates Chartered Surveyors Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Handicap

runners_data.name: Urban Road
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer on good ground (2W2P in similar conditions) but a 7yo who has finished 11th and 15th in his last two starts and drops back from 10f here; visor-wearing veteran whose best recent form came over further.

runners_data.name: Glorious Kitty
runners_data.note: Won two of her last five and is progressive at 4yo, with back-to-back wins over 7-8f on good ground suggesting this 1m trip is within range; Lewis Chalkley's 7lb claim is a significant weight-pull and she is the most natural horse to track Poet's Dawn in second.

runners_data.name: Up The Jazz
runners_data.note: Won over this exact trip on good ground last time out and clearly handles these conditions well (1W4P in similar going); hold-up style means he needs the pace to be genuine enough to pass horses, but his course-relevant form makes him a key player if he gets a clean run.

runners_data.name: Poet's Dawn
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner, 11yo but with two recent wins over 9-10f on good ground and clearly rejuvenated; David Allan is an experienced pilot to control pace from the front, and with no rival to press him, his ability to dictate terms makes him central to the entire race shape.

runners_data.name: Popeye Doyle
runners_data.note: Tongue-tied 4yo who finished 9th on good ground last time and has shown only one placed effort from six runs; hold-up style sits awkwardly in a field already overloaded with closers and his modest form figures give little confidence he can make an impact here.

runners_data.name: Jesmond Dawn
runners_data.note: Good recent form — 5th, 3rd and 2nd in last three outings — and Oisin Orr is an upgrade in the saddle; though his true running style is hold-up, he is pushed into a midfield map position by the overcrowded rear, meaning he cannot fully exploit his natural rhythm and the style-fit discount (0.93) tempers expectation.

runners_data.name: Hopeful Joy
runners_data.note: Absent 45 days and his last three runs on good ground produced a 7th, 3rd and 2nd, so the ability is there; a genuine hold-up horse by nature, but with four such types chasing the same space at the rear, he finds himself racing out of his preferred position and the style-fit flag (0.90) reflects the most meaningful fitness and positional concern in this field.

runners_data.name: Precious Spartan
runners_data.note: Long 89-day break is the obvious flag here, and his last run was a 9th at OR 64; despite solid historical form (3W4P in similar going) this is a horse rediscovering match practice, and his natural deep-closing style is further compromised by the redistribution that pushes him into midfield (style-fit 0.93).

runners_data.name: Volenti
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field at OR 51 and a 7yo who has not won in his last six; sits in midfield by redistribution rather than choice — his true preference is to race from the rear — and the combination of low rating, age and positional compromise (style-fit 0.91) make it hard to construct a compelling case.

races.paceDynamic: Poet's Dawn is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 1m handicap and, with no genuine rival to press him from the off, David Allan can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on good ground at Ripon. Glorious Kitty is the most likely horse to track him in second from a prominent pitch, with Urban Road, Up The Jazz and the redistributed hold-up horses settling further back in what will be a processional early order. The uncontested lead means the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which compresses the finish and makes it harder for genuine closers to generate meaningful momentum off a slow-run race. This race shape firmly favours horses who can race prominently or in the first three, as a lone front-runner controlling tempo on good ground at this track creates a significant advantage for those who sit close to the fractions — true hold-up horses are disadvantaged because four of them (Jesmond Dawn, Hopeful Joy, Precious Spartan and Volenti) could not all secure their natural rear position and are mapped into midfield, meaning the genuine closers this field contains are more likely to be caught in traffic than producing telling late runs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Poet's Dawn Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Poet's Dawn is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and sets a measured, controlled pace that rewards those racing prominently.
scenarios.body: Poet's Dawn dictates every fraction from the front, with Glorious Kitty the most likely to track and challenge in the straight, and the hold-up horses unable to generate the ground-cover needed from midfield. A controlled gallop on good ground at Ripon heavily rewards the front two and the closest prominent runner, making this the dominant and most likely race shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pegs Back Leader
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent or midfield tracker sustains a strong run from two furlongs out and overhauling Poet's Dawn in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: Glorious Kitty or Up The Jazz, sitting close to the pace throughout, finds enough in the tank to collar Poet's Dawn late as the leader's effort slightly flattens in the closing stages. This shape still suits horses racing prominently rather than from behind, and neither of the hold-up types likely to make the frame are true deep closers in this configuration.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Splits Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race and creates enough of a gap for one of the redistributed midfield horses to thread through and finish with purpose.
scenarios.body: Jesmond Dawn or Hopeful Joy, though not in their natural roles, capitalises if the field fans wide and a clear rail run materialises in the straight on good ground. The STYLE_FIT discounts for both horses acknowledge this is an against-the-grain shape and the probability is reduced accordingly — this only lands under specific circumstances.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Bunches The Field
scenarios.trigger: If Poet's Dawn crawls so slowly that the entire field concertinas and a sprint finish develops, eliminating any positional advantage.
scenarios.body: A sprint-finish scenario theoretically opens the race up, but the horses best placed to benefit — those with raw speed — are the same prominent types already covered in Scenario A and B. With most of the hold-up horses carrying REDISTRIBUTED tags and operating out of role, this shape produces few new winners and remains the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Glorious Kitty's jockey claim of 7lbs combined with her natural prominent style makes her the single biggest danger to Poet's Dawn — watch whether Lewis Chalkley elects to track the leader immediately from the break.

Poet's Dawn is 11 years old and has run four times in the last 18 days; watch for any signs of a flat or laboured stride in the final furlong that might suggest fatigue catching up with a busy campaign.

Up The Jazz won over this exact trip on good ground last time and is the most dangerous hold-up threat — watch whether Warren Fentiman (3lb claimer) can find a clear passage through the bunched midfield that this slow-pace scenario is likely to create.

Four genuinely hold-up horses (Jesmond Dawn, Hopeful Joy, Precious Spartan, Volenti) are all competing for the same limited late-running real estate — watch for traffic interference and scrimmaging in the straight if any of them attempt to challenge simultaneously from the same sector.

Precious Spartan returns from 89 days off for Patrick Neville, whose 14-day strike rate is just 1/8 — watch the market for any significant support that might suggest the yard has this horse cherry-ripe after a lengthy absence.

races.name: Mark's Choice, Ripon's Most-Winning Horse Handicap

runners_data.name: Vince L'Amour
runners_data.note: Won over 5f Good last time out (1st) and Tim Easterby's yard is firing at 7/98 in 14 days; travels prominently and is ideally positioned to stalk Goyard through the race before challenging in the final 100 yards, though the tongue-tie headgear is already factored into recent runs.

runners_data.name: Tees Aggregates
runners_data.note: Adrian Nicholls' four-year-old has remarkable 5f form on Good ground — three wins and four places from 15 similar-going starts — and Jack Nicholls (5lb claim) partners him fresh off a win 14 days ago; hold-up style means he needs the right trip through the field but has the raw form to land this off OR=73.

runners_data.name: Rock Of England
runners_data.note: Two of his last five runs produced wins on Good ground over 5f, and he returns from 33 days off for Paul Midgley who is notoriously patient with his horses; natural hold-up tendencies mean he will need a seam to open in the straight, but his course-distance profile is solid.

runners_data.name: Goyard
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner at OR=82 who will have first run on the field under Tudhope; he is the highest-rated horse here but the [STYLE_FIT=0.92] flag signals he is stretching to lead rather than racing from his more natural prominent position, and 142lbs top weight is a stiff ask in a handicap.

runners_data.name: Kodiac Thriller
runners_data.note: Visored for the first time today, which can sharpen focus, but his last five runs at 6f dominate his record and three of those show double-figure finishes on Good; the step back to 5f is the key question and his OR=80 looks flattering on current form.

runners_data.name: Reigning Profit
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's seven-year-old has run five consecutive times at 5f on Good-type ground, finishing 6-4-10-2-5, showing admirable consistency without winning; hold-up style suits a contested pace but this steady shape may leave him finishing into beaten horses.

runners_data.name: Mark's Choice
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's ten-year-old carries a peak/tongue-tie flag and genuine hold-up form, but with several natural closers in this field he will struggle to find his preferred rearward berth — his OR=69 and recent form (0624) make winning difficult even if the race unfolds perfectly.

runners_data.name: Canaria Queen
runners_data.note: Two wins and six places from 8 similar-going runs tells you she handles this surface well, and Tim Easterby's stable strike rate supports her; races prominently, handled with peak headgear, and her Good 5f form (1-2-2-1) is the strongest in-form reading in the field.

runners_data.name: South Parade
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey horse whose last five 5f runs on Good ground have produced finishes of 9-7-12-12 which makes the form hard to build a case around; a genuine hold-up type pushed into a midfield map position by field congestion, which further diminishes an already modest chance off OR=61.

races.paceDynamic: Goyard is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no meaningful challenger disputing the lead, Daniel Tudhope can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on a flat 5f Ripon track where Good going rewards those who travel comfortably. Vince L'Amour, Kodiac Thriller, and Canaria Queen will press for prominent positions, meaning the early stalls will be competitive, but none of them has the front-running credentials to genuinely pressurise Goyard into a suicidal pace. Mark's Choice and South Parade are genuine hold-up horses who have been mapped to midfield because the rear of this field is overcrowded with closers — they are unlikely to operate from their natural rearward pitch, which dilutes the threat of a true late sweep. This race shape — a single front-runner setting a honest but uncontested tempo on Good ground over a sprint — squarely favours horses who can travel prominently or just off the pace and deploy their finishing kick from a close-up position, rather than those reliant on a truly fast, pressured early gallop to generate the necessary gap for closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Goyard Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Goyard bowls along at his own pace and the prominent brigade tracks him into the straight.
scenarios.body: Tudhope sets a metronomic tempo, denying closers the strong early fractions they need, and a horse travelling comfortably in second or third takes over inside the final furlong as Goyard's high weight tells; Vince L'Amour and Tees Aggregates are best placed to capitalise, though Goyard's OR=82 gives him a margin of class.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Goyard's controlled tempo produces a falsely slow race and genuine closers find a clear route from the rear.
scenarios.body: The moderate fractions compress the field, and a horse with a sharp turn of foot can pick up late on the Good surface; Rock Of England, a proven front-runner who may find himself tracking rather than leading, is the most dangerous, while Reigning Profit's consistent 5f Good-ground form gives him each-way claims.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Sweep
scenarios.trigger: If Vince L'Amour or Canaria Queen push Goyard hard enough early to cause a pace collapse.
scenarios.body: A genuinely contested sprint burns off the pace brigade and opens the door for horses coming from further back; Tees Aggregates, with three wins and four places across 15 similar-going runs, has the finishing reserves to benefit, and Rock Of England's two 5f Good-ground wins underline his suitability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Redistributed Closers Profit
scenarios.trigger: If the field fans wide, traffic clears early, and Mark's Choice or South Parade can access their true hold-up position despite the crowded rear.
scenarios.body: This depends on those horses racing in their natural late-running style, which the field shape makes improbable; if it materialises, Canaria Queen's strong place form in similar conditions and Reigning Profit's proximity to the pace give them the better angles even in a scramble.

watchPoints.text: Canaria Queen — if Tim Easterby's mare breaks cleanly and secures the position just behind Goyard, her 5f Good-ground strike rate (two wins and multiple places in recent form) makes her a major player in the dominant scenario.

Goyard's weight — at 142lbs top weight for David O'Meara, watch whether Tudhope allows a true lead or whether a rival forces him to race too freely in the first two furlongs, which would turn the race shape from controlled to contested.

Kodiac Thriller's visor — first-time headgear on a horse with an inconsistent recent record can produce an unexpected forward show or alternatively a sharper early exit; monitor his position after the first furlong to assess its effect.

Rock Of England returns from a 33-day break with Paul Midgley, who has zero runners in the T14 window — the stable is not in a hot streak but Rock Of England's Good-ground 5f wins are genuine and he merits monitoring in the straight.

South Parade and Mark's Choice — if either drifts wide at the start and cannot access a clean hold-up position, their already diminished chances reduce further; watch the early stages for any crowding in the pack.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Handicap

runners_data.name: Picaro
runners_data.note: Races as a genuine hold-up horse with four runs all resulting in mid-field placings, has only one win/place on similar going (1 from 4) and the combination of 135lbs top weight and sole good-ground sample raises questions, but the 25-day freshen-up and Oisin Orr booking keep the interest alive.

runners_data.name: Vietnorm
runners_data.note: Three wins from his last five including back-to-back victories on Good ground, making him the form pick of the field; as a hold-up horse over 16f last time he is comfortable stretching out and the Keatley yard is operating at 2/18 in the past fortnight — modest, but the horse's own form does the talking.

runners_data.name: Fairydale
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's filly ran creditably for third over this 14f trip on Good last time out — the most relevant piece of form in the race — but she is a natural hold-up type that the map has pushed into midfield because the rear is overcrowded, meaning her chance depends on the race developing slowly enough to compensate.

runners_data.name: Keep It Classic
runners_data.note: Haggas-trained and handled by Tom Marquand, who is a strong booking; placed on Good ground at 12f suggesting the extra two furlongs here is workable, though the horse's natural style is hold-up and it will not get that position freely, trimming confidence slightly.

runners_data.name: Resdev Time
runners_data.note: Only 13 days since his last run and has posted five consecutive midfield finishes — consistency without a win — and while his Good-ground figures are acceptable (3 from 10), his true hold-up style displaced into midfield by the congested field reduces his scope to deliver a meaningful late run.

runners_data.name: Hansteen
runners_data.note: The 89-day layoff is a significant flag, and his three-run form string of 6-8-0 on varying ground including a non-completion is concerning; the ⚠ fade flag reinforces that this horse does not sustain his effort when the race gets serious, and John & Sean Quinn's yard is running cold at 1/12 in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Star Of Emerald
runners_data.note: The sole runner with an unknown style, which makes him the most likely accidental pace-setter in a field devoid of front-runners; has only one run on Good ground from five recorded (finishing 4th over 12f) and drops in trip slightly, so tactical uncertainty rather than form makes him the one to watch positionally from the gates.

runners_data.name: Riddikulus
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's 3-year-old has blinkers fitted and has placed four times at 4th but never won or placed in the top three; the 5lb claimer Rhys Elliott takes a practical advantage off in terms of weight, but on Good ground the horse has only one run from seven recent starts on that surface — the form and going profile both underwhelm.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in this eight-strong field, Star Of Emerald (unknown style) is the most likely candidate to find herself at the head of affairs by default, though the pace she sets is likely to be moderate at best over this 1m4f trip on Good turf at Ripon. The entire field is populated by hold-up operators, meaning the race will almost certainly drift through a slow-to-steady gallop before collapsing into a sprint finish in the straight — a shape that typically suits the freshest legs and the horse with the best turn of foot, not pure stayers grinding it out. Vietnorm brings strong form credentials (three recent wins) and genuine good-ground effectiveness, while Keep It Classic and Fairydale have shown the ability to place on this surface. This race shape heavily favours hold-up horses with a sharp finishing kick on Good ground, and runners who can produce a sustained late run rather than those who need to be delivered early — though the field holds more genuine hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear, meaning Fairydale, Keep It Classic, Resdev Time, Riddikulus and Hansteen cannot all achieve their natural position; the horses most likely to actually secure the rear-group slots are Vietnorm and Picaro, who have the firmest hold-up credentials backed by recent form.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish, Closers Win
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and the field bunches, producing a sprint-finish cavalry charge from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Star Of Emerald or whichever runner drifts to the front sets a dawdle, the entire field compresses, and the straight becomes a dash for home with position and foot-speed paramount. Vietnorm and Picaro, as the truest hold-up horses with the best recent going form, are ideally placed to unleash their finishing efforts in this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Good-Ground Traveller Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate gallop produces a genuine sustained stretch from two furlongs out, rewarding the horse with the best all-round form on Good ground.
scenarios.body: Vietnorm, who has won three times recently on Good ground and drops back to a trip within range of those wins, is the standout beneficiary as the field strings out in the straight. Keep It Classic, placed on Good ground over 12f, also profiles well as a horse whose style suits a gradually-run race that develops into a test.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sole Pace-Setter Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Star Of Emerald — or whichever runner assumes the lead by default — sets a comfortable solo gallop and is never seriously pressured.
scenarios.body: Without any confirmed front-runner to force a genuine pace, the default leader could pinch a decisive advantage by dictating a moderate tempo and conserving energy for a sustained effort in the straight at Ripon. Star Of Emerald (unknown style) is the most likely beneficiary here, having recently run over a similar trip on Good ground, and the lack of any horse naturally gunning for the lead increases the chance of a soft lead going unchallenged.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Midfield Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the horses mapped to midfield — truly a hold-up type racing out of its natural position — overcomes the style-fit discount and produces the best late run.
scenarios.body: Fairydale (blinkers, placed on Good ground over 14f) or Resdev Time (placed on Good ground, 13 days fresh) could benefit if the race develops slowly enough for them to creep into contention despite not securing their ideal rear position. The STYLE_FIT penalty dampens expectation here, but a falsely run race with a sprint finish could still bring one of them into the frame.

watchPoints.text: Vietnorm — if Barry McHugh can position him in a genuine hold-up berth and get a clear run from the home turn, his three recent wins on Good ground make him the most dangerous horse in the race when the sprint finish materialises.

Star Of Emerald — with no confirmed front-runner in the field, watch where Rowan Scott positions this unknown-style runner from the gates; if he drifts to the lead unchallenged, he could set a crawl that distorts the entire race shape.

Hansteen — the 89-day absence combined with a recorded fade flag and a non-completion in recent form means he could burn out early if he travels keenly into a slow gallop, potentially interfering with the run of horses behind him.

Keep It Classic — Tom Marquand's tactical intelligence is worth monitoring through the early stages; if he manages to find a prominent-but-covered position rather than being shuffled to the rear despite his hold-up label, his form on Good ground at 12f gives him live each-way claims.

Fairydale — blinkers are fitted and she ran well over this exact trip and going combination last time; watch whether David Allan elects to track the pace rather than drop her out, as doing so would mitigate the style-fit concern raised by her redistribution to midfield.

races.name: David Chapman Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: Mare Of London
runners_data.note: 306 days off the track is a significant concern for this hold-up filly, whose best recent form has come on Standard ground rather than Good; trainer George Scott has a modest 14-day strike rate and Ray Dawson will need to find plenty of late momentum in a race where the pace may not truly suit her deep style.

runners_data.name: Lamlash Bay
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby send this three-year-old out on a quick ten-day turnaround with Lewis Chalkley claiming; races prominently which is the ideal profile for the expected controlled pace here, though turf soft-and-standard form rather than Good does raise a minor going question.

runners_data.name: Soul Warrior
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's three-year-old carries a fade-in-finish flag and is a genuine hold-up type whose natural position at the rear is unlikely to be available in a field this congested with closers — expect Alex Jary to find a midfield slot at best, meaning this horse races in conditions that don't entirely suit its pattern.

runners_data.name: Brash
runners_data.note: David & Nicola Barron's sole confirmed front-runner here and the race-shaper; Oisin Orr can lead uncontested which suits the horse's style, though a style-fit flag notes it races mildly out of role as a promoted prominent, and Good ground form is thin with just one hit from three comparable starts.

runners_data.name: Hvar
runners_data.note: John & Sean Quinn's three-year-old has a desperately poor recent record — just one win from seven on Good ground and a string of double-figure finishes — and while Jason Hart is a class booking, this hold-up type needs a very different pace scenario to that expected here.

runners_data.name: Tie Fighter
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand rides for Ed Dunlop, a 2/16 trainer in the 14-day window, and this hold-up gelding wears a blindfold (b); Standard ground specialist whose five recorded runs include no Good-ground wins and two placed efforts on softer surfaces, making the going angle a mild positive concern for finding his best.

runners_data.name: Northern Tempest
runners_data.note: Michael Dods sends out this hold-up type on a 16-day break with the tongue-tie retained; placed three times on Good ground in recent form which is encouraging, but as a true back-end horse pushed into midfield by field congestion, Rhys Elliott's 5lb claim may not compensate for racing in a less natural position.

runners_data.name: Havana Oaks
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's filly has shown consistent placed form around 5-6f but all on Standard or Soft ground — this Good turf conditions represent an unknown quantity for her; a genuine hold-up type, she is among those squeezed out of her natural rear position by the volume of closers in the field.

runners_data.name: Long Shot
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's prolific operator (14/112 in 14 days) sends out this hold-up type wearing a hood on a 14-day return; Long Shot has been placed seven times on Good ground and has decent course-and-distance form, but as a true hold-up horse who will be pushed forward by field dynamics, David Allan must find a workable position in a tactically compressed race.

races.paceDynamic: Brash is the confirmed lone front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead identified in this field, Oisin Orr can dictate an uncontested, controlled tempo over Ripon's flat 6f on Good ground. That sustainable gallop will compress the race into a straight sprint-finish rather than a war of attrition, reducing the premium on stamina and rewarding horses who can land a challenge within two furlongs of home rather than those who need a truly searching pace to deliver their best from deep. Soul Warrior, Northern Tempest, Havana Oaks, and Long Shot are all genuine hold-up types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field holds more back-end runners than the shape can naturally accommodate at the rear — of those, Soul Warrior and Long Shot are most likely to actually secure a rear-midfield berth, but none will find the truly searching pace they need. This shape strongly favours prominent racers who can slot in behind Brash and pounce, or the rare hold-up horse quick enough to close on a modest gallop, though the tactical verdict leans clearly toward the prominent-to-midfield profile: horses who can track the controlled pace and respond in the final furlong without requiring a true end-to-end test.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Brash Dictates, Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Brash leads uncontested and sets a fair but unhurried pace, allowing a prominent or close-tracking rival to stalk and pick up.
scenarios.body: Brash rolls along at the front without pressure and the race develops as a tactical 6f contest where horses who can sit just off the pace hold the decisive positional advantage; the winner will emerge from behind the leader at the two-furlong pole and sustain their effort to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Brash Stays On To Win
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely modest and Brash's rivals fail to close, leaving him to score from the front under Orr.
scenarios.body: With no horse pressing Brash for the lead, he dictates every yard on his own terms and the hold-up horses — many not in their true position — cannot generate sufficient momentum to reel him in on Good ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late Blow
scenarios.trigger: If Brash's tempo is slow enough that the field compresses and the hold-up horses do find natural cover close enough to pounce.
scenarios.body: The race bunches into a sprint finish off a slow tempo, giving the redistributed closers — Soul Warrior or Long Shot — a slim but genuine window to arrive late if they secure a better-than-expected berth; the style-fit discount tempers confidence but the compressed field narrows the gap.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the race dissolves into a crawl and a complete outsider with fresh legs and a low draw benefits from positional chaos.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race on the flat Ripon track can produce a lottery finish where a lightly raced or well-handicapped runner like Hvar or Havana Oaks catches everyone flat-footed in the dash to the line; both are long shots, but the scenario's low likelihood makes this the province of the surprise result only.

watchPoints.text: Brash and Oisin Orr — if Brash jumps cleanly and gets to the front unchallenged inside the first furlong, the entire race shape locks in around him and prominent trackers become the primary beneficiaries.

Long Shot (hood, hold-up) and Soul Warrior (fade flag) are true closers being compressed into midfield — watch whether David Allan or Alex Jary can find clear daylight at the two-furlong pole, because a traffic-bound finish kills their chance entirely.

Mare Of London returns after 306 days off and has shown no proven ability to deliver after a long absence — if she is backward or slow to warm up through the first half of the race, discount her finishing effort regardless of her Going suitability.

Northern Tempest has placed three times on Good ground in recent starts, making it the most form-consistent of the redistributed hold-up types — monitor whether Rhys Elliott can secure a better-than-expected position off the pace in the early stages.

The entire field is rated between OR 52 and OR 65, an unusually narrow handicap band — any horse that gets a trouble-free run in a compressed field is capable of running into the places, making positional luck at the two-furlong pole a key race-reading factor.
